question: Should `openclaw/plugin-sdk/archive`, `openclaw/plugin-sdk/root-walk`, and `openclaw/plugin-sdk/secret-file` become supported public plugin SDK contracts, or should this work remain core-owned until a narrower API is approved?
rationale: The branch deliberately turns internal fs-safe capabilities into three new public extension interfaces; tests and generated API baselines establish consistency but cannot determine the intended permanent external contract.

options.title: Approve the three focused SDK seams
options.body: Treat the documented archive, root-walk, and secret-file subpaths as supported plugin APIs, then complete dependency publication and lockfile proof.

options.title: Keep the capabilities core-owned
options.body: Remove or defer the public exports and migrate only bundled callers through internal core facades until an owner-approved plugin contract is designed.

recommendation.title: Approve the three focused SDK seams
recommendation.body: Treat the documented archive, root-walk, and secret-file subpaths as supported plugin APIs, then complete dependency publication and lockfile proof.

likelyOwner.reason: This contributor owns the linked fs-safe integration work and can provide the technical contract rationale, while final API acceptance remains a repository maintainer decision.
